newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU prods Turkey on Cyprus dispute.
newsitem.headline: EU prods Turkey on Cyprus dispute.

text.p: The European Commission urged Turkey on Friday to work for a settlement to the dispute over Cyprus and said its external relations commissioner would visit the divided island to discuss EU membership with both sides.
Commissioner Hans van den Broek told Turkish Undersecretary for Foreign Affairs Onur Oymen that Turkey should join U.N.- brokered efforts to seek a solution, a Commission statement said.

"He urged Turkey to join in international efforts under the auspices of the United Nations to achieve a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus question in accordance with the U.N. Security Council resolutions based on the concept of a bi-communal and bizonal federation," it said.
Van den Broek told Oymen he would visit Cyprus on February 26-28 for talks with the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriots about preparations for Cyprus to join the European Union, it said.
The EU intends to begin membership negotiations with Cyprus six months after it finishes its inter-governmental review of its workings, which is scheduled to end in June at the EU's Amsterdam summit.

EU officials quoted Oymen as saying the Commission should rethink its stand on Turkey's own application for EU membership, having advised EU governments against opening talks with Ankara in 1989 because of its poor record on human rights.
Oymen said Turks believed that their country was not being treated equally with other candidate countries.

Van den Broek did not commit himself to revising the Commission's opinion. He said Turkey should submit a human rights programme and answer concerns expressed by EU foreign ministers over territorial disputes with Greece in the Aegean.
Turkey's relations with Greece, an EU member, have been severely strained over Cyprus and the mounting tension has led to fears that war could break out between the two NATO allies.
A Commission statement said the EU was looking to meeting between the EU and Turkish foreign affairs ministers on April 30 to make progress on normalising relations.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkish forces occupied the northern third of the island in 1974 after a coup by the military then ruling Greece.
